2027-01-29.title: Friday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Do not abandon that confidence of yours
The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord
The seed grows, he does not know how; the mustard seed
2027-01-29.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 3 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green.
2027-01-29.verse: He also said, “The kingdom of God is as if someone would scatter seed on the ground, and would sleep and rise night and day, and the seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.
theo: Hebrews reminds a tired community of its early courage: “Recall those earlier days when, after you had been enlightened, you endured a hard struggle with sufferings… you cheerfully accepted the plundering of your possessions.” Now they are tempted to give up. “Do not, therefore, abandon that confidence of yours; it brings a great reward. For you need endurance.” Faith is not only a beginning; it is a long faithfulness. “We are not among those who shrink back and so are lost, but among those who have faith and so are saved.”

Jesus gives two small parables that are a medicine for discouragement. A farmer scatters seed, sleeps and rises, “and the seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.” The earth produces “first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain in the head.” And the mustard seed, “the smallest of all the seeds on earth”, becomes a shrub where the birds nest. God's Kingdom grows quietly, slowly and surely, often while we sleep. Our part is to sow faithfully and to trust; the growth belongs to God.
outline: Ask: have you ever planted something and waited impatiently?
Point 2 · The seed grows by itself
“The seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.”
live: Keep going with one good thing you are tempted to give up.
Do one small act of faith today and leave the results to God.
2027-01-29.prayer: Lord God, your Kingdom grows like seed in the night and like the smallest of seeds. Give us endurance not to shrink back, patience to sow and wait, and trust that you give the growth. Amen.
altar: A small piece of bread becomes the Body of Christ; the smallest seeds of God's Kingdom are planted in us at every Communion.

quick: Do not abandon your confidence; you need endurance.
The seed grows by itself; God gives the growth.
The mustard seed becomes a great shrub.
2027-01-29.action: Keep going with one good thing you are tempted to give up.
2027-01-29.question: Where am I tempted to shrink back?

family.explain: A mustard seed is tiny, but it grows into a big plant where birds can sit. Small good things we do for God can grow big!
family.intention: We pray for people who are tired and want to give up.
family.ask: Ask: “What small good thing can each of us do today?”

illus: A widow in Kottayam ran a tiny Sunday school class of four children in her verandah for twenty years. She never saw big results. At her funeral three priests and two religious sisters came; all had been in her class. One said: she planted a mustard seed and slept; God made it grow.

pm.open: Lord, give us patience and endurance as we sow the seed of your Kingdom. Amen.
share: Do not abandon that confidence of yours (Hebrews 10:35). Where am I losing heart?
He does not know how (Mark 4:27). Do I trust God with what I cannot see?
The smallest of all the seeds (Mark 4:31). What small thing can I offer?
interc: For those who are tired and discouraged.
For parents and teachers who sow faith in children.
For persecuted Christians who need endurance.
For our group, that we may persevere.
pm.close: Father, you give the growth. Make us faithful sowers and patient waiters. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews speaks to a tired community: recall those earlier days when, after you had been enlightened, you endured a hard struggle with sufferings (Hebrews 10:32). Now they were tempted to give up.
Do not, therefore, abandon that confidence of yours; it brings a great reward. For you need endurance (Hebrews 10:35–36). Faith is a long faithfulness.

Jesus gives two small parables for the discouraged. The seed grows, he does not know how (Mark 4:27). The mustard seed, the smallest of all seeds, becomes a great shrub (Mark 4:31–32). God's Kingdom grows quietly and surely.
Our part is to sow faithfully and to trust. The growth belongs to God. Do not shrink back. Amen.
kids: Children, a tiny mustard seed grows into a big plant! Small kind things we do for Jesus can grow into something big.

intro: Theme: “The seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.”
Endurance, patience and the quiet growth of God's Kingdom.

q: Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the LORD!
Do not, therefore, abandon that confidence of yours; it brings a great reward.
points.apply: Persevere in one good habit this week.

q: Commit your way to the LORD; trust in him, and he will act.
So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but only God who gives the growth.
points.apply: Leave one worry about results with God.

q: On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, in order that it may produce boughs and bear fruit, and become a noble cedar. Under it every kind of bird will live; in the shade of its branches will nest winged creatures of every kind.
It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown upon the ground, is the smallest of all the seeds on earth;
points.apply: Do one small act of faith and trust God with it.

concl: God's Kingdom grows quietly and surely.
2027-01-29.resolve: Do not give up a good work you have begun.
